tools.name: read_job_posting
tools.description: Reads the job posting at a link and returns its title, company and text, so you can see what the job asks for before tailoring the person's résumé to it. Use it when the person shares a link to a job. Reads public job pages only; some sites can't be read, and then it says so.

tools.name: tailor_resume
tools.description: BetterShell's resume builder. Makes the person a finished, tailored one-page résumé PDF from their own résumé or CV: it picks their strongest material for the job, rewrites their bullets toward the job's language without inventing anything, puts the job's key terms on the page where their experience

tools.name: review_resume
tools.description: Measures the person's résumé the way BetterShell lays out a page and returns the facts for a review: how much of a page it fills, which jobs have one line, lines with no number or result, lines that open with what they were assigned rather than what they did, lines that run long, missing contact det

tools.name: read_resume
tools.description: Returns the text of a résumé BetterShell made, line by line with ids, as it prints. Use it to talk about the résumé, write or change a line the person asks for, write a follow-up or a cover note from what was sent, or prepare them for an interview.

tools.name: edit_resume
tools.description: Changes lines, the summary or the look of a résumé BetterShell made, fits it back to its page and redraws it, with a new PDF. Use it when the person asks to reword, shorten, add or remove a line, or to see another look. You write the new words, from the person's own facts; read_resume gives the line

tools.name: make_cover_letter
tools.description: Prints a cover letter you wrote as the pair of a résumé BetterShell made: the same header, type and colours, fitted to one page, with a PDF. Write it from what the résumé and the person say, never adding a claim the résumé doesn't support (read_resume gives its text), then send the paragraphs here w

tools.name: connect_bettershell_account
tools.description: Connects the person's BetterShell account, so the résumés BetterShell makes in this chat are made on that account and saved there, where they can edit, download and tailor them later. Optional: use it when the person asks to use their BetterShell account. Making a résumé doesn't need it.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Returns the person's saved BetterShell profile: every job, project and activity with its lines, and their skills, in their own words. Use it to ask about their work one job at a time, to see what a job needs that the profile lacks, or to search for jobs that fit it.

tools.name: add_to_profile
tools.description: Saves what the person tells you to save to their BetterShell profile, in their own words: lines under a job, project or activity, a new entry, or skills. Nothing already there is repeated. Use it only for what they asked to save; every résumé BetterShell makes after can use it.

tools.name: list_applications
tools.description: Shows the person's applications in BetterShell and the stage each reached, with how many got a phone screen or an interview, which have waited for a reply, and repeats at one employer. Use it when they ask how their search is going or what to follow up on.

tools.name: update_application
tools.description: Records news on one of the person's applications when they tell you: they applied, had a phone screen or an interview round, got an offer or a rejection, or withdrew.

tools.name: interview_prep
tools.description: For one application, returns the page that was sent, the person's own lines that page left off, and the posting, to prepare them for that interview from what the employer will be holding.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Checks a job posting against the person's saved profile, measured the way BetterShell makes the page: whether there is a full page of material for it, and which tools and terms the posting names that the profile never does. Use it on postings the person shares or that you found for them.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: review_resume · Private data: review_resume, update_application · Public sink: make_cover_letter · Destructive: review_resume, edit_resume.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: review_resume · Private data: review_resume, update_application · Public sink: make_cover_letter · Destructive: review_resume, edit_resume

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
